claims.statement: The Nguruvilu is a legendary creature of the Mapuche religion of Chile's indigenous people.
claims.statement_id: Nguruvilu adalah makhluk legenda dari agama Mapuche, penduduk asli Chile.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature originating from the Mapuche religion of the indigenous people inhabiting Chile.

claims.statement: It lives in lakes or rivers, with a fox-like head and a snake-like body.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di danau atau sungai, berkepala mirip rubah dan bertubuh mirip ular.
claims.quote: It is a lake- or river-dwelling creature that appears in the form with a fox-like head and snake-like body

claims.statement: It snatches waders with its long clawed tail and devours or drains its victims.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyambar orang yang mengarungi air dengan ekor panjangnya yang bercakar, lalu memangsa atau mengisap darah korbannya.
claims.quote: which snatches wading people with its (clawed) long tail, and devours or blood-sucks its victim.

claims.statement: Its etymology is "fox" + "serpent".
claims.statement_id: Etimologinya adalah "rubah" + "ular".
claims.quote: The etymology is given as "fox" + "serpent"

claims.statement: This led the natives to avoid bathing in lakes where it lives.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu penduduk asli menghindari mandi di danau tempat makhluk ini berada.
claims.quote: causing the natives to avoid bathing in the lakes where the beast occurs.

claims.statement: Besides Nguruvilu, the creature is also called Guruvilu, Guirivilu and Guirivilo.
claims.statement_id: Selain Nguruvilu, makhluk ini disebut juga Guruvilu, Guirivilu, dan Guirivilo.
claims.quote: The Nguruvilu or Guruvilu, Guirivilu, Guirivilo, etc.,

claims.statement: Nguruvilus live in dangerous whirlpools that kill people trying to cross rivers; they make the water shallow on either ford so that crossing seems safe.
claims.statement_id: Nguruvilu hidup di pusaran air berbahaya yang membunuh orang yang mencoba menyeberangi sungai; mereka membuat air dangkal di kedua sisi arungan agar penyeberangan tampak aman.
claims.quote: Nguruvilus live in dangerous whirlpools which kill people who try to cross rivers. The creatures make the water shallow on either ford, to encourage people to try to cross it making it seem safe.

claims.statement: Later sources describe the nguruvilu with the face of a puma or wildcat and a clawed tail (or many claws).
claims.statement_id: Sumber-sumber yang lebih belakangan menggambarkan nguruvilu berwajah puma atau kucing liar dengan ekor bercakar (atau banyak cakar).
claims.quote: Later sources describe the nguruvilu with the face of a puma or wildcat and a clawed tail (or many claws).

claims.statement: For a layman, the only way to get rid of a nguruvilu is through a machi (shaman) or a good kalku (sorcerer).
claims.statement_id: Bagi orang awam, satu-satunya cara menyingkirkan nguruvilu adalah lewat jasa seorang machi (dukun) atau kalku (penyihir) yang baik.
claims.quote: (For a layman), the only way to get rid of a nguruvilu is through the offices of a machi (shaman) or good kalku "sorcerer".

claims.statement: The kalku (male or female) wades through the river to the whirlpool and dives in, then swims to the surface having captured the Nguruvilu in their arms with powerful magical abilities.
claims.statement_id: Kalku (laki-laki atau perempuan) mengarungi sungai sampai ke pusaran lalu menyelam, kemudian berenang ke permukaan sambil memeluk Nguruvilu yang ditangkapnya dengan kemampuan sihirnya.
claims.quote: The kalku (who may be male or female) wades through the river until they reach the whirlpool and then dives in. Afterwards, they swim to the surface having captured the Nguruvilu in their arms with their powerful magical abilities.

claims.statement: Lehmann-Nitsche (1902) wrote that, according to his informant Nahuelpi, the fox-viper was believed to do no harm so long as a certain form of worship was performed.
claims.statement_id: Lehmann-Nitsche (1902) menulis bahwa menurut informannya, Nahuelpi, ular-rubah dipercaya tidak mencelakai selama orang menjalankan bentuk ibadah tertentu.
claims.quote: Lehmann-Nitsche (1902) wrote that according to his informant Nahuelpi, it was believed that the fox-viper did no harm so long as they performed a certain form of worship.

claims.statement: It was taboo to call it by name, and the circumlocution "lord of the water" was used.
claims.statement_id: Memanggil namanya langsung dianggap tabu, dan sebutan lain "penguasa air" dipakai sebagai gantinya.
claims.quote: It was taboo to call it by name, and the circumlocution "lord of the water" was used.

claims.statement: Anthropologist Robert Lehmann-Nitsche was of the opinion that the myth of this creature originated from observations of the otter, specifically the marine otter Lutra felina.
claims.statement_id: Antropolog Robert Lehmann-Nitsche berpendapat bahwa mitos makhluk ini berasal dari pengamatan terhadap berang-berang, khususnya berang-berang laut Lutra felina.
claims.quote: Anthropologist Robert Lehmann-Nitsche was of the opinion that the myth of this creature originated from observations of the otter, more particularly Lutra felina G. I. Molina, i.e. marine otter

claims.statement: Some described it as fox-headed with a serpent's body, but others claimed it was like a round, bloated ox hide.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian menggambarkannya berkepala rubah dan bertubuh ular, tetapi yang lain menyebutnya seperti kulit lembu yang bundar dan menggembung.
claims.quote: Some described it as fox-headed with the body of a serpent (as its name suggests), but others claimed it was like a round bloated ox hide

claims.statement: According to the Mapuche sourced by Tomás Guevara (1908), it is a river-dwelling beast with a cat-like head, a small slender body and an extremely long fox-like tail.
claims.statement_id: Menurut orang Mapuche yang menjadi narasumber Tomás Guevara (1908), ia binatang sungai berkepala mirip kucing, bertubuh kecil dan ramping, dengan ekor sangat panjang seperti rubah.
claims.quote: a river-dwelling beast with a cat-like head, a small and slender body, and an extremely long tail like the fox's, according to the Mapuche sourced by ethnologist Tomás Guevara (1908)

claims.statement: A mythology dictionary describes a monster half fox and half serpent that usually lives in muddy waters.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kamus mitologi memerikan monster setengah rubah setengah ular yang biasanya hidup di perairan berlumpur.
claims.quote: mitad zorro y mitad serpiente que suele vivir en aguas cenagosas

claims.statement: In local mythology, the Pincoya is a female water spirit of the Chilotan seas.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitologi setempat, Pincoya adalah roh air perempuan dari laut Chiloé.
claims.quote: The Pincoya is, according to local mythology, a female "water spirit" of the Chilotan Seas.

claims.statement: The Pincoya has long blond hair and incomparable beauty, is cheerful, and rises from the sea's depths.
claims.statement_id: Pincoya konon berambut pirang panjang, sangat cantik, ceria, dan muncul dari kedalaman laut.
claims.quote: The Pincoya is said to have long blond hair, be of incomparable beauty, be cheerful and sensual, and rise from the depths of the sea.

claims.statement: She personifies the fertility of marine species.
claims.statement_id: Ia melambangkan kesuburan makhluk laut.
claims.quote: Naked and pure, she personifies the fertility of marine species.

claims.statement: If she dances facing the sea, fish will be plentiful; facing the mountains, seafood will be scarce.
claims.statement_id: Jika ia menari menghadap laut, pantai itu akan berlimpah ikan; jika menghadap gunung, hasil laut akan langka.
claims.quote: If she performs her dance facing the sea, it means that these shores will have an abundance of fish.  When she dances facing the mountains, her back to the sea, seafood will be scarce.

claims.statement: Other legends make her the daughter of Millalobo, king of the sea, and the human Huenchula.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda lain, Pincoya putri Millalobo, raja laut, dan Huenchula, seorang manusia.
claims.quote: According to other legends, Pincoya is the daughter of Millalobo (king of sea, in chilote mythology) and the human Huenchula.

claims.statement: Her sister is the Sirena chilota and her brother Pincoy, who is also her husband.
claims.statement_id: Saudarinya Sirena chilota, dan saudaranya Pincoy, yang juga suaminya.
claims.quote: Her sister is the Sirena chilota (a type of Mermaid) and her brother is Pincoy (who also is her husband).

claims.statement: The three siblings guide drowned sailors onto the phantom ship Caleuche.
claims.statement_id: Ketiga bersaudara itu menuntun pelaut yang tenggelam ke kapal hantu Caleuche.
claims.quote: The three siblings lead and guide the drowned sailors onto a large phantom ship, the Caleuche

claims.statement: She is described with a naked body, hair between reddish and blond, and beautiful feminine lines.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan bertubuh telanjang, berambut antara kemerahan dan pirang, dengan lekuk tubuh perempuan yang indah.
claims.quote: PINCOYA: f. ... Su cuerpo desnudo, su cabellera entre rojiza y rubia, y sus hermosas lineas femeninas

claims.statement: The enchantresses with their powers kept her under their control and, through sowings and other rituals, made the Pincoya fertilize a beach, an estuary or a fishing or shellfish site.
claims.statement_id: Para encantadoras dengan kekuatannya dianggap mengendalikannya dan, lewat penaburan dan ritual lain, membuat Pincoya menyuburkan pantai, muara, atau tempat menangkap ikan dan kerang.
claims.quote: Las encantadoras con sus poderes la mantenian bajo su control y, mediante siembras ... y otros rituales, lograban que la Pincoya fertilizara una playa, un estero o un sitio de pesca o marisca.

claims.statement: Unlike the Sirena, the Pincoya has no fish tail.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dengan Sirena, Pincoya tidak berekor ikan.
claims.quote: PINCOYA: f. ... A diferencia de la Sirena, ... no posee cola de pescado.

claims.statement: The Pincoya is a protective patroness of the shellfish and fish of the coast.
claims.statement_id: Pincoya adalah pelindung kerang-kerangan dan ikan di pesisir.
claims.quote: PINCOYA: f. Patrona protectora de ... mariscos y peces de la costa.

claims.statement: Chiloean mythology is appreciative of the Pincoya, who is believed to be good, beautiful and humanitarian.
claims.statement_id: Mitologi Chiloé menghargai Pincoya, yang dipercaya baik, cantik, dan peduli pada sesama manusia.
claims.quote: Chiloean mythology is appreciative of the Pincoya, believed to be good, beautiful and humanitarian.

claims.statement: The ship appears briefly intact with sounds of a party on board but quickly vanishes; myth has it that once on board the dead can resume an existence as if alive.
claims.statement_id: Kapal itu tampak utuh sebentar dengan suara pesta di atasnya lalu cepat lenyap; menurut mitos, setelah naik ke kapal orang mati dapat hidup kembali seolah masih hidup.
claims.quote: The ship appears briefly intact with sounds of a party on board, but quickly vanishes. Myth has it that, once on board, the dead can resume an existence as if they were alive again.

claims.statement: Qiqirn is a large, bald dog spirit of Inuit mythology from around Baffin Island.
claims.statement_id: Qiqirn adalah roh anjing besar tak berbulu dalam mitologi Inuit dari sekitar Pulau Baffin.
claims.quote: Qiqirn is a large, bald dog spirit in Inuit mythology, from around the area of Baffin Island.

claims.statement: It has hair only on its feet, mouth and ear and tail tips; its presence sends men and dogs into sometimes fatal convulsions.
claims.statement_id: Bulunya hanya ada di kaki, mulut, serta ujung telinga dan ekor; kehadirannya membuat manusia dan anjing kejang, kadang sampai mati.
claims.quote: It has hair only on its feet, mouth and the tips of its ears and tail. Its presence will send men and dogs into convulsions, sometimes fatal.

claims.statement: But it fears humans and runs away if an angakkuq sees it.
claims.statement_id: Namun ia takut pada manusia dan akan lari jika dilihat angakkuq (dukun).
claims.quote: However, it is frightened of humans and will run away if an angakkuq sees it.

claims.statement: Daniel Merkur suggested the fits it causes allude to shamanic initiations.
claims.statement_id: Daniel Merkur menduga kejang akibat qiqirn adalah kiasan untuk inisiasi dukun.
claims.quote: Daniel Merkur suggested that the fits caused by the qiqirn were allusions to shamanic initiations.

claims.statement: In Rudyard Kipling's short story "Quiquern" it is a giant, phantasmal, toothless, hairless dog with six or eight pairs of legs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerpen Rudyard Kipling "Quiquern", makhluk ini digambarkan sebagai anjing hantu raksasa tanpa gigi dan bulu dengan enam atau delapan pasang kaki.
claims.quote: In Rudyard Kipling's short story "Quiquern", the creature is described as a giant, phantasmal, toothless and hairless dog with six or eight pairs of legs.

claims.statement: A similar term, also from Inuit mythology, is keelut, a malevolent earth spirit that also appears as a hairless dog.
claims.statement_id: Istilah serupa dari mitologi Inuit adalah keelut, roh bumi jahat yang juga tampil sebagai anjing tak berbulu.
claims.quote: A similar term, also from Inuit mythology, is keelut, a malevolent earth spirit which also appears as a hairless dog.

claims.statement: In the story "Quiquern", Quiquern is the phantom of a gigantic toothless, hairless dog said to live in the far North and to wander the country just before things are going to happen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita "Quiquern", Quiquern adalah hantu anjing raksasa tak bergigi dan tak berbulu yang konon hidup di Utara yang jauh dan berkeliaran tepat sebelum suatu peristiwa terjadi.
claims.quote: Quiquern, too, is the phantom of a gigantic toothless dog without any hair, who is supposed to live in the far North, and to wander about the country just before things are going to happen.

claims.statement: In the story, not even the sorcerers care to speak about Quiquern, and he makes the dogs go mad.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita itu, bahkan para dukun tidak mau membicarakan Quiquern, dan ia membuat anjing-anjing menjadi gila.
claims.quote: but not even the sorcerers care to speak about Quiquern. He makes the dogs go mad.

claims.statement: In the story, the girl, sobbing with laughter, pushes the two shamefaced creatures towards Kotuko and cries that this is Quiquern, who led them to safe ground, with eight legs and a double head.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita itu, sang gadis sambil terisak tertawa mendorong dua makhluk yang malu itu ke arah Kotuko dan berseru bahwa itulah Quiquern yang menuntun mereka ke tanah aman, dengan delapan kaki dan kepala ganda.
claims.quote: The girl pushed the two shamefaced creatures towards Kotuko, and, sobbing with laughter, cried, “That is Quiquern, who led us to safe ground. Look at his eight legs and double head!”

claims.statement: In the story, each of the pair was fastened sidelong to the other's neck, and this, with the freedom of hunting on their own account, must have helped to cure their madness.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita itu, masing-masing dari pasangan tersebut terikat menyamping pada leher temannya, dan hal itu bersama kebebasan berburu sendiri tentu membantu menyembuhkan kegilaan mereka.
claims.quote: each was fastened sidelong to his neighbour’s neck. That, with the freedom of hunting on their own account, must have helped to cure their madness.

claims.statement: Two young Inuit hunters, desperate to find food for their starving tribe, believe they are guided by Quiquern, only to discover that the many-legged "spirit" is actually a pair of sled dogs whose collars had become entangled.
claims.statement_id: Dua pemburu Inuit muda yang putus asa mencari makanan untuk sukunya yang kelaparan mengira dituntun Quiquern, lalu mendapati "roh" berkaki banyak itu ternyata sepasang anjing penarik kereta yang kalungnya terjerat.
claims.quote: Two young Inuit hunters, desperate to find food for their starving tribe, believe they are being guided by Quiquern, only to discover that the many-legged "spirit" is actually a pair of sled dogs whose collars had become entangled.

claims.statement: In Arizona folklore, the Red Ghost is a figure said to have roamed the Arizona frontier in the late 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Arizona, Red Ghost adalah sosok yang konon berkeliaran di perbatasan Arizona pada akhir abad ke-19.
claims.quote: In Arizona folklore, the Red Ghost is a figure alleged to have roamed the Arizonan frontier in the late 19th century.

claims.statement: It was said to be a large red camel with a bleached human skeleton on its back.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon unta merah besar dengan kerangka manusia yang memutih di punggungnya.
claims.quote: It was said to have been a large red camel with a bleached human skeleton upon its back.

claims.statement: Background: War Secretary Jefferson Davis's proposal to use camels was approved in 1855 in what became the Camel Corps.
claims.statement_id: Latar belakangnya: usulan Menteri Perang Jefferson Davis untuk memakai unta disetujui pada tahun 1855 dalam eksperimen yang kemudian dikenal sebagai Camel Corps.
claims.quote: with a proposal by then Secretary of War Jefferson Davis ultimately being approved in 1855 with a budget of $30,000 in an experiment that would later become known as the Camel Corps.

claims.statement: The legend began in 1883, when two men left their ranch house near Eagle Creek.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini bermula pada tahun 1883, ketika dua pria meninggalkan rumah peternakan mereka dekat Eagle Creek.
claims.quote: The legend began in 1883, when two men left their ranch house near Eagle Creek to check on their cattle.

claims.statement: On returning, they found one wife trampled to death.
claims.statement_id: Sepulangnya, mereka mendapati salah satu istri mereka tewas terinjak-injak.
claims.quote: When the two men returned, they found the other's wife had been trampled to death.

claims.statement: In 1893, The Mohave County Miner reported on what is now an Arizona legend: the Red Ghost, a rampant camel with a dead man strapped to its back.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1893, The Mohave County Miner memberitakan legenda Arizona yang kini dikenal: Red Ghost, unta mengamuk dengan mayat terikat di punggungnya.
claims.quote: In 1893, The Mohave County Miner reported on what is now an Arizona legend: the Red Ghost, a rampant camel with a dead man strapped to its back.

claims.statement: A hunter named Si Hamlin caught sight of the Red Ghost from a distance and reported he thought that the thing on its back was the body of a dead man.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pemburu bernama Si Hamlin melihat Red Ghost dari kejauhan dan melaporkan bahwa ia mengira benda di punggungnya adalah tubuh orang mati.
claims.quote: A hunter named Si Hamlin caught sight of the Red Ghost from a distance and reported he thought that something was the body of a dead man.

claims.statement: When a priest named Mizoo Hastings finally shot it, he found the camel's back knotted with rawhide straps that had presumably once held on a corpse, by now disintegrated.
claims.statement_id: Ketika seorang pastor bernama Mizoo Hastings akhirnya menembaknya, ia mendapati punggung unta itu terikat tali kulit mentah yang tampaknya dulu menahan sesosok mayat yang kini sudah hancur.
claims.quote: When a priest named Mizoo Hastings finally shot it, he found the camel’s back had been knotted with rawhide straps, presumably once holding on a corpse that had by now disintegrated.

claims.statement: The legend remained popular until 1893, when farmer Mizoo Hastings found the creature eating in his yard and shot it dead with a single shot.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini tetap populer sampai 1893, ketika petani Mizoo Hastings mendapati makhluk itu makan di halamannya lalu menembaknya hingga mati dengan satu tembakan.
claims.quote: The legend remained popular until 1893, when farmer Mizoo Hastings found the creature eating in his yard and proceeded to shoot it, killing it in a single shot.

claims.statement: Though the newspaper claimed sightings had been reported for ten years before the camel's death at Mr. Hastings's hands, there is no trace of earlier reports.
claims.statement_id: Meski surat kabar itu menyebut penampakan sudah dilaporkan selama sepuluh tahun sebelum unta itu mati di tangan Hastings, tidak ada jejak laporan yang lebih awal.
claims.quote: Though the newspaper claimed sightings had been reported for ten years before the camel’s death at Mr. Hastings’s hands, there is no trace of earlier reports.

claims.statement: Camels did briefly roam the deserts of Arizona, set loose after the 1863 dissolution of the US Camel Corps, an army experiment in using camels to carry explorers and supplies through southwestern deserts.
claims.statement_id: Unta memang sempat berkeliaran di gurun Arizona setelah dilepaskan pascabubarnya US Camel Corps pada 1863, eksperimen militer memakai unta untuk mengangkut penjelajah dan perbekalan melintasi gurun barat daya.
claims.quote: Camels did briefly roam the deserts of Arizona, having been set loose in the aftermath of the 1863 dissolution of the US Camel Corps, an army experiment in using camels to carry explorers and supplies through southwestern deserts.

claims.statement: The author suggests the Red Ghost may well have been a remnant of dissolved government plans or business enterprise hopes.
claims.statement_id: Penulis menduga Red Ghost bisa jadi sisa dari rencana pemerintah yang dibubarkan atau harapan usaha dagang tersebut.
claims.quote: Our Red Ghost may well have been a remnant of either of these dissolved government plans or business enterprise hopes.

claims.statement: Some posit that the corpse was a prospector dying of thirst who tied himself to the camel's back hoping it would lead him to water, while others allege a soldier was learning to ride a camel when it suddenly bolted off.
claims.statement_id: Ada yang menduga mayat itu seorang pendulang yang sekarat kehausan dan mengikat dirinya ke punggung unta dengan harapan unta menuntunnya ke air, sementara yang lain menyebut seorang prajurit yang sedang belajar menunggang unta ketika hewan itu tiba-tiba kabur.
claims.quote: with some positing that the corpse was that of a prospector dying of thirst who tied himself to the camel's back, hoping that the animal would lead him to water, while others alleged that a soldier was learning to ride a camel when the animal suddenly bolted off.

claims.statement: One tale described the creature killing and eating a grizzly bear and another said it disappeared into thin air when chased, but the skeleton of a man on its back was a common element across the stories.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah menggambarkan makhluk itu membunuh dan memakan beruang grizzly, kisah lain menyebut ia lenyap ke udara saat dikejar, tetapi kerangka manusia di punggungnya menjadi unsur umum dalam kisah-kisah itu.
claims.quote: one described the creature killing and eating a grizzly bear, while another said it disappeared into thin air when chased, but the skeleton of a man on its back was a common element among the stories

claims.statement: In one sighting the creature was described as 30 feet tall and knocking over two wagons.
claims.statement_id: Pada satu penampakan, makhluk itu digambarkan setinggi 30 kaki dan menggulingkan dua gerobak.
claims.quote: this time being described as 30 feet (9.1 m) tall and knocking over two wagons

claims.statement: A sculpture of the camel was erected in Quartzsite, Arizona, near the grave of Hi Jolly, an Ottoman camel driver who worked for the Camel Corps.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah patung unta itu didirikan di Quartzsite, Arizona, di dekat makam Hi Jolly, pengemudi unta Utsmaniyah yang bekerja untuk Camel Corps.
claims.quote: A sculpture of the camel was erected in Quartzsite, Arizona, near the grave of Hi Jolly, an Ottoman camel driver who worked for the Camel Corps.

claims.statement: The snallygaster is a bird-reptile chimera from the folklore of early German immigrants in what is now Frederick County, Maryland.
claims.statement_id: Snallygaster adalah makhluk campuran burung dan reptil dari cerita rakyat imigran Jerman awal di wilayah yang kini Frederick County, Maryland.
claims.quote: The snallygaster is a bird-reptile chimera originating in the folklore of early German immigrants who settled in the region of what is now Frederick County, Maryland.

claims.statement: In the early 20th century its legends were revived by sensational newspaper reports.
claims.statement_id: Pada awal abad ke-20, legendanya dihidupkan kembali oleh laporan surat kabar yang sensasional.
claims.quote: In the early 20th century, legends of the Snallygaster were revived through sensationalistic newspaper reports

claims.statement: Early accounts describe a monster called Schneller Geist, "quick ghost" in German.
claims.statement_id: Kisah awal menyebut masyarakat diteror monster bernama Schneller Geist, yang dalam bahasa Jerman berarti "hantu cepat".
claims.quote: Early accounts describe the community being terrorized by a monster called a Schneller Geist, meaning "quick ghost" in German.

claims.statement: It was described as half reptile, half bird, with a metallic beak lined with razor-sharp teeth.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan setengah reptil setengah burung, berparuh logam dengan gigi setajam silet.
claims.quote: The snallygaster was described as being half-reptile and half-bird, possessing a metallic beak lined with razor-sharp teeth.

claims.statement: It reportedly swooped silently from the sky to carry off its victims.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon menukik diam-diam dari langit untuk menyambar dan membawa pergi korbannya.
claims.quote: The snallygaster was rumored to swoop silently from the sky to pick up and carry off its victims.

claims.statement: The earliest stories claim the monster sucked the blood of its victims; seven-pointed stars, which reputedly kept the snallygaster at bay, can still be seen painted on local barns.
claims.statement_id: Kisah-kisah paling awal menyebut monster ini menghisap darah korbannya; bintang bersudut tujuh, yang konon menjaga snallygaster tetap jauh, masih terlihat dicat di lumbung setempat.
claims.quote: The earliest stories claim that this monster sucked the blood of its victims. Seven-pointed stars, which reputedly kept the snallygaster at bay, can still be seen painted on local barns.

claims.statement: It was also said to have octopus-like tentacles.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini juga dikatakan memiliki tentakel seperti gurita.
claims.quote: It was also said to have octopus-like tentacles.

claims.statement: Newspaper accounts throughout February and March 1909 describe encounters between residents and a beast with enormous wings, a long pointed bill, claws like steel hooks and an eye in the center of its forehead.
claims.statement_id: Laporan surat kabar sepanjang Februari dan Maret 1909 menggambarkan perjumpaan warga dengan binatang bersayap sangat besar, berparuh panjang runcing, bercakar seperti kait baja, dan bermata satu di tengah dahi.
claims.quote: Newspaper accounts throughout February and March 1909 describe encounters between local residents and a beast with "enormous wings, a long pointed bill, claws like steel hooks, and an eye in the center of its forehead."

claims.statement: It was later revealed that these reports were part of a hoax by Middletown Valley Register editor George C. Rhoderick and reporter Ralph S. Wolfe to increase readership.
claims.statement_id: Belakangan terungkap bahwa laporan-laporan itu bagian dari tipuan editor Middletown Valley Register George C. Rhoderick dan reporter Ralph S. Wolfe untuk menaikkan jumlah pembaca.
claims.quote: It was later revealed that these reports were part of a hoax perpetrated by Middletown Valley Register editor George C. Rhoderick and reporter Ralph S. Wolfe in an attempt to increase readership.

claims.statement: Early sightings led to a particular association with the Frederick County areas of South Mountain, Braddock Heights and the Middletown Valley.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan awal mengaitkan makhluk ini terutama dengan kawasan South Mountain, Braddock Heights, dan Middletown Valley di Frederick County.
claims.quote: Early sightings led to a particular association with the Frederick County areas of South Mountain, Braddock Heights, and the Middletown Valley.

claims.statement: Reports of the Snallygaster, a strange beast prowling the woods of Frederick County, have been made since the 1730s, making it one of Maryland's oldest legends.
claims.statement_id: Laporan tentang Snallygaster, binatang aneh yang berkeliaran di hutan Frederick County, sudah ada sejak 1730-an sehingga menjadi salah satu legenda tertua Maryland.
claims.quote: Reports of the Snallygaster, a strange beast prowling the woods of Frederick County, have been made since the 1730s, making it one of Maryland’s oldest legends.

claims.statement: Eighteenth-century accounts by the early German settlers refer to the beast as a Schneller Geist, or quick ghost, that rapidly pounced upon its unsuspecting prey.
claims.statement_id: Catatan abad ke-18 para pemukim Jerman awal menyebut binatang itu Schneller Geist atau "hantu cepat" yang menerkam mangsanya yang tak curiga dengan cepat.
claims.quote: 18th-century accounts by the early German settlers refer to the beast as a Schneller Geist or quick ghost that rapidly pounced upon its unsuspecting prey.

claims.statement: In December 1932 the Hagerstown Morning Herald reported the death of the Snallygaster, purportedly lured to a moonshine still in Frog Hollow in Washington County, overcome by the noxious fumes and drowned in the alcoholic vat.
claims.statement_id: Pada Desember 1932, Hagerstown Morning Herald memberitakan kematian Snallygaster: konon ia dipancing ke alat penyulingan minuman keras ilegal di Frog Hollow, Washington County, dan tewas karena asapnya lalu tenggelam di bak alkohol.
claims.quote: Then, in December 1932, the Hagerstown Morning Herald reported on the death of the Snallygaster. It was purportedly lured to a moonshine still in Frog Hollow in Washington County and was overcome by the noxious fumes and drowned in the alcoholic vat.

claims.statement: Some have suggested that the accounts beginning in 1909 were a veiled attempt at scaring away would-be ne'er-do-wells from Middletown and the surrounding region.
claims.statement_id: Ada yang menduga laporan sejak 1909 adalah upaya terselubung menakut-nakuti calon pembuat onar agar menjauh dari Middletown dan sekitarnya.
claims.quote: Some have suggested that the accounts beginning in 1909 were a veiled attempt at scaring away would be ne’er-do-wells from Middletown and the surrounding region.

claims.statement: Others explain that the original letter from T.C. Harbaugh is the explanation, as Thomas Chalmers Harbaugh was a native of Middletown and an accomplished author with a passion for the area's history and culture.
claims.statement_id: Yang lain menjelaskan bahwa surat asli T.C. Harbaugh-lah penyebabnya, karena Thomas Chalmers Harbaugh adalah warga asli Middletown dan penulis mumpuni yang mencintai sejarah dan budaya kawasan itu.
claims.quote: Others have explained that the original letter from T.C. Harbaugh is the explanation – as Thomas Chalmers Harbaugh was a native of Middletown and an accomplished author with a passion for the area’s history and culture.

claims.statement: The Tlahuelpuchi is a legendary vampiric witch of Tlaxcala, Mexico, rooted in Nahua culture.
claims.statement_id: Tlahuelpuchi adalah penyihir pengisap darah dalam cerita rakyat negara bagian Tlaxcala, Meksiko, yang berakar pada budaya Nahua.
claims.quote: The Tlahuelpuchi is a legendary vampiric witch in folklore from the Mexican state of Tlaxcala, with deep roots amongst the indigenous Nahua culture of the region.

claims.statement: Thus tlahuelpuchi may mean "glowing haze" or "illuminated youth".
claims.statement_id: Karena itu, tlahuelpuchi dapat berarti "kabut bercahaya" atau "pemuda yang diterangi".
claims.quote: As a result, tlahuelpuchi may mean glowing haze or illuminated youth.

claims.statement: It can shapeshift and sucks the blood of infants at night.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat berubah wujud dan mengisap darah bayi pada malam hari.
claims.quote: It is able to shape shift and sucks the blood of infants at night.

claims.statement: Tlahuelpuchi are born with their curse and learn of it around puberty.
claims.statement_id: Tlahuelpuchi lahir dengan kutukannya dan tak bisa menghindarinya; mereka baru menyadarinya sekitar masa puber.
claims.quote: Tlahuelpuchi are born with their curse and cannot avoid it. They first learn of what they are sometime around puberty.

claims.statement: Tlahuelpuchi must feed on blood at least monthly or die.
claims.statement_id: Tlahuelpuchi harus mengisap darah sedikitnya sebulan sekali atau mati.
claims.quote: Tlahuelpuchi must feast on blood at least once a month or they die.

claims.statement: Garlic, onions and metal repel the tlahuelpuchi.
claims.statement_id: Bawang putih, bawang merah, dan logam mengusir tlahuelpuchi.
claims.quote: Garlic, onions and metal repel the tlahuelpuchi.

claims.statement: The dictionary translates tlahuipochtli as "sorcerer or animal spirit", sometimes paired with nahualli, and lists tlahuelpuchi among its orthographic variants.
claims.statement_id: Kamus itu menerjemahkan tlahuipochtli sebagai "penyihir atau roh hewan", kadang dipasangkan dengan nahualli; tlahuelpuchi tercantum sebagai salah satu variannya.
claims.quote: Headword: tlahuipochtli. Principal English Translation: sorcerer or animal spirit, sometimes paired with nahualli (see attestations) Orthographic Variants: tlahuipochin, tlahuihpochtli, tlahuihpochin, tlahuelpuchi

claims.statement: The dictionary cites tlahuipochtin as those who walked about at night spitting fire and causing madness, sickness or death in their victims.
claims.statement_id: Kamus itu mengutip tlahuipochtin sebagai mereka yang berjalan-jalan pada malam hari, menyemburkan api dan menyebabkan kegilaan, sakit, atau kematian pada korbannya.
claims.quote: tlahuipochtin = those who walked about at night "spitting fire and causing madness, sickness, or death in their victims"

claims.statement: The dictionary also refers to the tlahuelpuchi/tlahuepoche, or "fiery red smoke", in Tlaxcala and the Sierra Poblana.
claims.statement_id: Kamus itu juga menyebut tlahuelpuchi/tlahuepoche, atau "asap merah menyala", di Tlaxcala dan Sierra Poblana.
claims.quote: In reference to the tlahuelpuchi/tlahuepoche or “fiery red smoke” in Tlaxcala and the Sierra Poblana

claims.statement: Tlahuelpuchi can change form by detaching their body from their legs, which are left in the witch's house, and then go hunting, usually as a bird such as a turkey or a vulture.
claims.statement_id: Tlahuelpuchi dapat berubah wujud dengan melepaskan tubuh dari kakinya (yang ditinggalkan di rumah si penyihir), lalu berburu, biasanya dalam wujud burung seperti kalkun atau burung nasar.
claims.quote: Tlahuelpuchi are able to change form by detaching their body from their legs (which are left in the house of the witch). They then go hunting, usually in the form of some bird like a turkey or a vulture.

claims.statement: The tlahuelpuchi must fly over the house in the shape of a cross, from north to south and east to west.
claims.statement_id: Tlahuelpuchi harus terbang di atas rumah membentuk salib, dari utara ke selatan dan timur ke barat.
claims.quote: The tlahuelpuchi must fly over the house in the shape of a cross from north to south, east to west.

claims.statement: Most tlahuelpuchi are female, and female tlahuelpuchi are more powerful than males.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar tlahuelpuchi adalah perempuan, dan tlahuelpuchi perempuan lebih kuat daripada yang laki-laki.
claims.quote: Most tlahuelpuchi are female and the female tlahuelpuchi are more powerful than males.

claims.statement: A tlahuelpuchi cannot be detected except by catching them in the act; their family protects them out of shame and because the curse passes to a family member responsible for a tlahuelpuchi's death.
claims.statement_id: Tlahuelpuchi tidak bisa dikenali kecuali tertangkap basah; keluarganya melindunginya karena malu dan karena kutukan akan berpindah kepada anggota keluarga yang bertanggung jawab atas kematiannya.
claims.quote: There is no way to detect a tlahuelpuchi except by catching them in the act. Their family protects them out of shame and because if a family member is responsible for the death of a tlahuelpuchi the curse will be passed down to them.

claims.statement: The curse cannot be lifted, and if a tlahuelpuchi is identified they must be killed on the spot.
claims.statement_id: Kutukan itu tidak dapat dicabut, dan jika seorang tlahuelpuchi teridentifikasi, ia harus dibunuh di tempat.
claims.quote: The curse cannot be lifted, and if a tlahuelpuchi is identified, they must be killed on the spot.

claims.statement: On page 28 of the Codex Borgia, five Tlaloque water maize fields with different rains, only one of them beneficial.
claims.statement_id: Pada halaman 28 Codex Borgia, lima Tlaloque digambarkan menyirami ladang jagung dengan jenis hujan berbeda, dan hanya satu yang bermanfaat.
claims.quote: On page 28 of the Codex Borgia, the Five Tlaloque are pictured watering maize fields. Each Tláloc is pictured watering the maize with differing types of rains, of which only one was beneficial.

claims.statement: The Atlcahualo festival (12 February–3 March) was dedicated to the Tlaloque and involved child sacrifice on sacred peaks such as Cerro Tláloc.
claims.statement_id: Perayaan Atlcahualo (12 Februari–3 Maret) dipersembahkan kepada Tlaloque dan melibatkan pengorbanan anak-anak di puncak gunung suci seperti Cerro Tláloc.
claims.quote: The Atlcahualo festivals was celebrated from 12 February until 3 March. Dedicated to the Tlaloque, this veintena involved the sacrifice of children on sacred mountaintops, like Cerro Tláloc.

claims.statement: The winter veintena of Atemoztli (9–28 December) was also dedicated to the Tlaloque.
claims.statement_id: Veintena musim dingin Atemoztli (9–28 Desember) juga dipersembahkan kepada Tlaloque.
claims.quote: The winter veintena of Atemoztli (9 December – 28 December) was also dedicated to the Tlaloque.

claims.statement: The summit precinct holds five stones thought to represent Tláloc and his four Tlaloque, who provide rain for the land.
claims.statement_id: Di puncak Cerro Tláloc terdapat lima batu yang diduga melambangkan Tláloc dan empat Tlaloque-nya, yang bertugas memberi hujan bagi tanah.
claims.quote: The precinct on the summit of the mountain contains 5 stones which are thought to represent Tláloc and his four Tlaloque, who are responsible for providing rain for the land.

claims.statement: Tláloc was also considered the ruler of the Tlaloque, a motley group of rain, weather and mountain gods.
claims.statement_id: Tláloc juga dianggap penguasa Tlaloque, sekelompok dewa hujan, cuaca, dan gunung yang beraneka ragam.
claims.quote: Tláloc was also considered the ruler of the Tlaloque - a motley group of rain, weather and mountain gods

claims.statement: The dictionary translates Tlaloque as deities associated with rain and with Tlaloc, the deity of rain and celestial waters.
claims.statement_id: Kamus itu menerjemahkan Tlaloque sebagai dewa-dewa yang berkaitan dengan hujan dan dengan Tlaloc, dewa hujan dan air langit.
claims.quote: Headword: Tlaloque. Principal English Translation: deities, associated with rain and with Tlaloc, the deity of rain and celestial waters

claims.statement: In the text the dictionary quotes, these gods were called Tlalocs, and clouds, rain, hail, snow, mist, sheet lightning, thunder and lightning bolts that struck men were attributed to them.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip kamus itu, dewa-dewa ini disebut Tlalocs, dan kepada mereka dikaitkan awan, hujan, hujan es, salju, kabut, kilat lembaran, guntur, dan sambaran petir yang mengenai manusia.
claims.quote: These [gods] were called Tlalocs. To them were attributed clouds, rain, hail, snow, mist, sheet lightning, thunder, and lighting bolts which struck men.

claims.statement: Other tlaloque are Nappatecuhtli, Opochtli, Tomiyauhtecuhtli (one of the four hundred rabbits that were deities of pulque), and the tepictoton, small legless figures.
claims.statement_id: Tlaloque lain adalah Nappatecuhtli, Opochtli, Tomiyauhtecuhtli (salah satu dari empat ratus kelinci, dewa pulque), dan tepictoton, sosok kecil tanpa kaki.
claims.quote: Other tlaloque are Nappatecuhtli, Opochtli, Tomiyauhtecuhtli (one of the four hundred rabbits that were deities of pulque), and the tepictoton, small legless figures.

claims.statement: The Tlaloques were "rain dwarfs", lesser deities associated with various climatological phenomena such as snow, sleet and lightning.
claims.statement_id: Tlaloque disebut "kurcaci hujan", yaitu dewa-dewa yang lebih rendah yang dikaitkan dengan berbagai gejala cuaca seperti salju, hujan es, dan petir.
claims.quote: The Tlaloques were "rain dwarfs"; namely, lesser deities associated with various climatological phenomena such as snow, sleet, and lightning.

claims.statement: The ceremonial relationship between human beings and the Tlaloques was primarily based on food exchange.
claims.statement_id: Hubungan upacara antara manusia dan Tlaloque terutama berdasar pertukaran makanan.
claims.quote: The ceremonial relationship between human beings and the Tlaloques was primarily based on food exchange.

claims.statement: The wekufe is an important kind of harmful spirit or demon in Mapuche mythology; the word comes from Mapudungun wekufü, "demon, outside being".
claims.statement_id: Wekufe adalah jenis roh jahat atau iblis penting dalam mitologi Mapuche; kata ini berasal dari wekufü dalam bahasa Mapudungun, "iblis, makhluk dari luar".
claims.quote: is an important type of harmful spirit or demon in Mapuche mythology. The word wekufe comes from the Mapudungun word wekufü meaning "demon, outside being".

claims.statement: The word became tied to demons only after Catholicism brought the Mapuche the concept of evil.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini baru dikaitkan dengan iblis setelah Katolik datang dan orang Mapuche mengenal konsep kejahatan.
claims.quote: It was only after the arrival of Catholicism when the Mapuche people had gained the concept of evil that the word became associated with demons.

claims.statement: It is generally a generic name for Mapuche mythical beings with harmful intentions toward humans.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini umumnya dipakai sebagai sebutan umum bagi makhluk mitologi Mapuche yang berniat jahat kepada manusia.
claims.quote: The word is generally used as a generic name in order to describe creatures from Mapuche mythology that usually have harmful intentions towards human beings.

claims.statement: They thus cause illness, destruction, death and other calamities among the Mapuche.
claims.statement_id: Dengan demikian mereka menyebabkan penyakit, kehancuran, kematian, dan bencana lain di kalangan Mapuche.
claims.quote: In this way they cause illness, destruction, death, and other calamities amongst the Mapuche.

claims.statement: The evil forces are called wekufe and are of three major types: natural phenomena, ghosts, and those of zoomorphic form.
claims.statement_id: Kekuatan jahat disebut wekufe dan terdiri dari tiga jenis utama: fenomena alam, hantu, dan yang berwujud hewan.
claims.quote: The evil forces are called wekufe and are of three major types: natural phenomena, ghosts, and those of zoomorphic form.

claims.statement: Among contemporary Araucanians there are two kinds of sickness: one caused by supernatural agents, the wekufe and the perrimontu, and the other by natural agents or environmental factors.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan orang Araucania masa kini ada dua jenis penyakit: yang disebabkan agen gaib, yaitu wekufe dan perrimontu, dan yang disebabkan faktor alam atau lingkungan.
claims.quote: Among contemporary Araucanians, however, there are two kinds of sickness: one caused by supernatural agents, the wekufe and the perrimontu, and the other by natural agents or environmental factors.

claims.statement: The forces of evil are activated when envious people ask kalkus to use the evil spirits to attack the persons they envy.
claims.statement_id: Kekuatan jahat diaktifkan ketika orang yang iri meminta kalku memakai roh jahat untuk menyerang orang yang menjadi sasaran iri mereka.
claims.quote: The forces of evil are activated when envious people ask kalkus to use the evil spirits to attack persons who are the objects of their envy.

claims.statement: The Mapuche believe that many wekufes allow themselves to be manipulated by kalkus (Mapuche sorcerers, equivalent to witches or wizards who work with black magic), who use them as a mystic medium for obtaining power.
claims.statement_id: Orang Mapuche percaya banyak wekufe membiarkan diri dimanfaatkan kalku (penyihir Mapuche, setara penyihir yang memakai ilmu hitam), yang menjadikan mereka perantara mistik untuk memperoleh kekuatan.
claims.quote: The Mapuche believe that many wekufes allow themselves to be manipulated by kalkus (Mapuche sorcerers, equivalent to witches or wizards who work with black magic), who use them as a mystic medium for obtaining power.

claims.statement: Unlike other living beings or spirits that possess their own soul, wekufes are soulless.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dengan makhluk hidup atau roh lain yang memiliki jiwa sendiri, wekufe tidak berjiwa.
claims.quote: Unlike other living beings or spirits that possess their own soul, wekufes are soulless.

claims.statement: The best known of the wekufes are Trelke-wekufe (El Cuero or cow hide) and Canillo, both powerful wekufes able to change into solid form.
claims.statement_id: Wekufe yang paling terkenal adalah Trelke-wekufe (El Cuero atau kulit sapi) dan Canillo, keduanya wekufe kuat yang mampu berubah menjadi wujud padat.
claims.quote: The best known of the wekufes are Trelke-wekufe (El Cuero or cow hide), and Canillo, both of which are powerful wekufes with the ability to change into solid form.

claims.statement: The wekufe also have the power to capture and enslave the pillú (spirit of the recently deceased that is reluctant to leave its body) before it transforms into an alwe (more mature spirit).
claims.statement_id: Wekufe juga mampu menangkap dan memperbudak pillú (roh orang yang baru meninggal dan enggan meninggalkan tubuhnya) sebelum berubah menjadi alwe (roh yang lebih matang).
claims.quote: The wekufe also have the power to capture and enslave the pillú (spirit of the recently deceased that is reluctant to leave its body) before it transforms into an alwe (more mature spirit).

claims.statement: The machitún ceremony must be performed in order to release the wekufe.
claims.statement_id: Upacara machitún harus dilakukan untuk melepaskan wekufe.
claims.quote: The machitún ceremony must be performed in order to release the wekufe.

claims.statement: In the more southerly regions it was said that the wekufe, serving the Pillán and bringing disease to the hut (ruca), the cattle and the fields, could only be exorcised by burning foiqe or cinnamon branches.
claims.statement_id: Di wilayah yang lebih ke selatan dikatakan wekufe yang melayani Pillán dan membawa penyakit ke pondok (ruca), ternak, dan ladang hanya dapat diusir dengan membakar cabang foiqe atau kayu manis.
claims.quote: In the more southerly regions, it was said that the wekufe, serving the Pillán, bringing disease to the hut (ruca), the cattle, and the fields could only be exorcised by burning the foiqe or cinnamon branches.

claims.statement: Wekufes entered the Mapu world as a consequence of the mythical battle amongst the Pillán spirits, which resulted in the breaking of the Admapu.
claims.statement_id: Wekufe memasuki dunia Mapu sebagai akibat pertempuran mitos di antara roh-roh Pillán, yang mengakibatkan rusaknya Admapu.
claims.quote: Wekufes entered the Mapu world as a consequence of the mythical battle amongst the Pillán spirits, which resulted in the breaking of the Admapu

claims.statement: Mapuche legends say that wekufes come from Minchenmapu, located to the west beyond Mapu.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Mapuche menyebut wekufe berasal dari Minchenmapu, yang terletak di sebelah barat di seberang Mapu.
claims.quote: Mapuche legends say that wekufes come from Minchenmapu, which is located to the west beyond Mapu

claims.statement: As long as the Mapuche obey the admapu laws and perform the guillatún ceremony, the Ngen and Pillán spirits will continue to keep the wekufe under control.
claims.statement_id: Selama orang Mapuche menaati hukum admapu dan menjalankan upacara guillatún, roh Ngen dan Pillán akan terus mengendalikan wekufe.
claims.quote: As long as the Mapuche people obey the admapu laws and perform the guillatún ceremony, then the Ngen and Pillán spirits will continue to keep the wekufe under control.

claims.statement: In the Mapuche language, Mapudungun, the word wekufe can be attributed to any person who tells lies or is deceptive.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Mapuche, Mapudungun, kata wekufe dapat dikenakan pada siapa pun yang berbohong atau menipu.
claims.quote: In the Mapuche language, Mapudungun, the word wekufe can be attributed to any person that tells lies or is deceptive.

claims.statement: The werejaguar was both an Olmec motif and a supernatural being, perhaps a deity.
claims.statement_id: Werejaguar adalah motif seni Olmec sekaligus makhluk gaib, mungkin dewa.
claims.quote: The werejaguar was both an Olmec motif and a supernatural entity, perhaps a deity.

claims.statement: The motif has almond-shaped eyes, a downturned open mouth and a cleft head.
claims.statement_id: Motif werejaguar bercirikan mata berbentuk almon, mulut terbuka yang menurun, dan kepala terbelah.
claims.quote: The werejaguar motif is characterized by almond-shaped eyes, a downturned open mouth, and a cleft head.

claims.statement: It was once thought the main Olmec deity but is now seen as one of many.
claims.statement_id: Werejaguar pernah dianggap dewa utama Olmec, tetapi kini dianggap hanya salah satu dari banyak dewa.
claims.quote: The werejaguar supernatural was once considered to be the primary deity of the Olmec culture but is now thought to be only one of many.

claims.statement: Many scholars first tied it to a myth of a jaguar mating with a woman.
claims.statement_id: Awalnya banyak ahli mengira werejaguar terkait mitos perkawinan jaguar dengan perempuan.
claims.quote: Originally, many scholars believed that the werejaguar was tied to a myth concerning a copulation between a jaguar and a woman.

claims.statement: The term comes from Old English were ("man") and jaguar.
claims.statement_id: Istilahnya berasal dari kata Inggris Kuno were ("manusia") dan jaguar.
claims.quote: The term is derived from Old English were, meaning "man", and jaguar

claims.statement: The essential elements of the Were-Jaguar or Jaguar-Baby are the V-shaped cleft, clawed or paw-like feet or hands, and a feline head with, in some cases, a tail.
claims.statement_id: Unsur utama Were-Jaguar atau Jaguar-Baby adalah belahan berbentuk V, kaki atau tangan bercakar atau seperti cakar, dan kepala kucing yang dalam beberapa kasus berekor.
claims.quote: The essential elements of the Were-Jaguar or Jaguar-Baby are, the ‘V’ shaped cleft, clawed or paw like feet or hands and a feline head with, in some cases, a tail.

claims.statement: One view: the jaguar was a "power animal" of a shaman caste and stood for a "spirit journey", recalling a shared religious experience.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu pandangan: jaguar adalah "hewan kekuatan" kasta dukun dan melambangkan "perjalanan roh" yang mengingatkan pada pengalaman keagamaan bersama.
claims.quote: that the jaguar was a “power animal” of a shaman caste and stood for a “spirit journey,” recalling a shared religious experience

claims.statement: Another view: the Olmec believed themselves to be descended from the jaguar.
claims.statement_id: Pandangan lain: orang Olmec meyakini diri mereka keturunan jaguar.
claims.quote: that the Olmec believed themselves to be descended from the jaguar.

claims.statement: Another view: the jaguar was a representative tool functioning as a symbol of the dominance of the ruling class.
claims.statement_id: Pandangan lain: jaguar adalah alat representasi yang berfungsi sebagai lambang dominasi kelas penguasa.
claims.quote: that the jaguar was a representative tool, functioning as a symbol of the dominance of the ruling class

claims.statement: These representations come in a variety of forms: delicate greenstone figurines, votive axes, incised celts and large basalt sculptures.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran ini muncul dalam berbagai bentuk: patung batu hijau yang halus, kapak persembahan, kapak batu bergores, serta patung basal besar.
claims.quote: These representations come in a variety of forms; delicate greenstone figurines, votive axes (with the forms realised in 3 dimensions) and incised celts as well as large basalt sculptures

claims.statement: According to archaeologist Peter Furst, werejaguar figurines were likely used as household gods for many people and as spirit helpers or familiars for priests or shamans, aiding in transformative acts and other rituals.
claims.statement_id: Menurut arkeolog Peter Furst, patung werejaguar kemungkinan dipakai sebagai dewa rumah tangga bagi banyak orang dan sebagai pembantu roh bagi pendeta atau dukun dalam tindakan transformasi dan ritual lain.
claims.quote: According to archaeologist Peter Furst, werejaguar figurines were likely used as household gods for many people and as spirit helpers or familiars for priests or shamans, aiding in transformative acts and other rituals.

claims.statement: Some researchers have therefore refined the werejaguar supernatural, specifically equating it with the Olmec rain deity.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian peneliti karena itu mempersempit makhluk gaib werejaguar dengan menyamakannya secara khusus dengan dewa hujan Olmec.
claims.quote: Some researchers have therefore refined the werejaguar supernatural, specifically equating it with the Olmec rain deity

claims.statement: An overarching werejaguar theory cannot explain the diversity and complexity of Olmec supernaturals; only one, the Rain Baby, clearly seems to be a human-jaguar blend.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu pendapat ilmiah, teori menyeluruh werejaguar tidak dapat menjelaskan keragaman dan kerumitan makhluk gaib Olmec; hanya satu, Rain Baby, yang jelas tampak sebagai perpaduan manusia dan jaguar.
claims.quote: An overarching [werejaguar] theory cannot explain the diversity and complexity of Olmec supernaturals. Only one, the Rain Baby, clearly seems to be a human-jaguar blend.

claims.statement: Peter Furst, among others, has suggested that the werejaguar actually represents a variety of native toad.
claims.statement_id: Peter Furst, antara lain, mengusulkan bahwa werejaguar sebenarnya mewakili sejenis kodok asli setempat.
claims.quote: Peter Furst, among others, has suggested that the werejaguar actually represents a variety of native toad

claims.statement: Yacumama (Quechua, "mother of water") is an enormous mythical serpent believed to inhabit the Amazon rainforest.
claims.statement_id: Yacumama (dari bahasa Quechua, "ibu air") adalah ular raksasa mitos yang dipercaya menghuni hutan hujan Amazon.
claims.quote: Yacumama (from Quechua for "mother of water"), is a mythical enormous serpent believed to inhabit the Amazon Rainforest.

claims.statement: Legend makes it the mother of all aquatic animals, sucking in any living thing within 100 steps.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ia ibu semua hewan air dan mengisap makhluk hidup apa pun yang lewat dalam jarak 100 langkah.
claims.quote: According to legend, it is considered the mother of all aquatic animals and would suck up any living thing that passed within 100 steps of it.

claims.statement: For protection, local Indigenous people blew a conch before entering the water, believing the Yacumama would reveal itself.
claims.statement_id: Untuk melindungi diri, penduduk asli meniup terompet kerang sebelum masuk air karena percaya Yacumama akan menampakkan diri jika ada.
claims.quote: To protect themselves, local Indigenous peoples would blow on a conch horn before entering the water, believing that the Yacumama would reveal itself if it were present.

claims.statement: In the region that is home to the Shipibo-Conibo, Ashanika and Aguaruna peoples, a dangerous mythical anaconda, Yakumama, guards and protects the waters of the Amazon River.
claims.statement_id: Di kawasan yang dihuni orang Shipibo-Conibo, Ashanika, dan Aguaruna, seekor anakonda mitos yang berbahaya, Yakumama, menjaga dan melindungi perairan Sungai Amazon.
claims.quote: This region is home to the Shipibo-Conibo, Ashanika, and Aguaruna peoples. Here, a dangerous mythical anaconda, Yakumama, guards and protects the waters of the Amazon River.

claims.statement: The name Yakumama comes from the Quechua words yaku (agua) and mama (mother), meaning the Mother of Water.
claims.statement_id: Nama Yakumama berasal dari kata Quechua yaku (agua) dan mama (ibu), yang berarti Ibu Air.
claims.quote: The name Yakumama comes from the Quechua words yaku (agua) and mama (mother), meaning the Mother of Water.

claims.statement: In one tale, because of a fisherman's unwelcome presence, Yakumama created a whirlpool from which it emerged, putting the boat and the fisherman in immense danger.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu kisah, karena kehadiran seorang nelayan yang tidak diinginkan, Yakumama membuat pusaran air tempat ia muncul, sehingga perahu dan nelayan itu berada dalam bahaya besar.
claims.quote: Due to the man’s unwelcome presence, Yakumama created a whirlpool from which it emerged, putting the boat and the fisherman in immense danger.

claims.statement: The myth of Yacumama speaks of the respect owed to the forest and all living beings in it; the anaconda is the silent power that protects the forest's natural equilibrium and should not be disturbed.
claims.statement_id: Mitos Yacumama berbicara tentang rasa hormat yang harus diberikan kepada hutan dan semua makhluk hidup di dalamnya; anakonda adalah kekuatan senyap yang menjaga keseimbangan alam hutan dan tidak boleh diganggu.
claims.quote: The myth of Yacumama talks about the respect that must be paid to the forest and all living beings that are part of it. The anaconda is the silent power that protects the natural equilibrium of the forest and should not be disturbed.

claims.statement: In one story the great snake answered that its lament was because future generations would not respect and protect the rainforest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, ular besar itu menjawab bahwa ratapannya disebabkan generasi mendatang tidak akan menghormati dan melindungi hutan hujan.
claims.quote: the great snake responded that the lament was because future generations were not going to respect and protect the rainforest.

claims.statement: The Anchimayen is a Mapuche mythical creature in the form of small children that can turn into bright flying fireballs.
claims.statement_id: Anchimayen adalah makhluk mitos Mapuche berwujud anak kecil yang dapat berubah menjadi bola api terbang bercahaya terang.
claims.quote: is a mythical creature in Mapuche mythology. Anchimayens are described as little creatures that take the form of small children, and can transform into flying fireballs that emit bright light.

claims.statement: They are servants of a kalku, a type of Mapuche sorcerer.
claims.statement_id: Mereka pelayan kalku, sejenis penyihir Mapuche.
claims.quote: They are the servants of a kalku (a type of Mapuche sorcerer).

claims.statement: Anchimayens are sometimes confused with Kueyen, the Mapuche moon goddess, who also gives bright light.
claims.statement_id: Anchimayen kadang disamakan dengan Kueyen, dewi bulan Mapuche, karena sama-sama memancarkan cahaya terang.
claims.quote: Anchimayens are sometimes confused with Kueyen (the Mapuche lunar goddess), because she also produces a bright light.

claims.statement: The anchimallén are said to be heard like the crying of a newborn baby.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan anchimallén terdengar seperti tangisan bayi yang baru lahir.
claims.quote: Se dice que se les escucharía como el llanto de un bebe recién nacido

claims.statement: The anchimallén is said to feed on milk, blood or honey, its mission being to protect and obey its owner, doing good or evil according to the wishes of whoever controls it.
claims.statement_id: Anchimallén dikatakan makan susu, darah, atau madu, dan tugasnya melindungi serta menaati pemiliknya, berbuat baik atau jahat sesuai keinginan pengendalinya.
claims.quote: El anchimallén se alimentaría con leche, sangre o miel, siendo la misión del anchimallén la de proteger y obedecer a su dueño haciendo el bien o el mal; según los deseos de quién lo controla.

claims.statement: The calcu is said to create them from the remains of a girl or boy who died suddenly.
claims.statement_id: Sang calcu dikatakan menciptakan mereka dari jasad seorang anak perempuan atau laki-laki yang meninggal mendadak.
claims.quote: El calcu los crearía a partir de los restos mortales perteneciente a una niña o un niño que murió de una forma repentina.

claims.statement: If someone sees it up close, the anchimallén is said to use its light to confuse and disorient, leaving the person momentarily stunned or even blind, with sick eyes, one-eyed or stuttering.
claims.statement_id: Bila seseorang melihatnya dari dekat, anchimallén dikatakan memakai cahayanya untuk membingungkan dan menyesatkan, membuat orang itu terpana sesaat atau bahkan buta, sakit mata, picak, atau gagap.
claims.quote: el anchimallén utilizaría su luz para confundir y desorientar, dejando aturdido momentáneamente a la persona; o incluso dejándola ciega, enferma de la vista o tuerta o tartamuda.

claims.statement: It is said that only Machitún ceremonies and a good machi can make this being escape from the body.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan hanya upacara Machitún dan seorang machi yang baik yang dapat mengeluarkan makhluk ini dari tubuh.
claims.quote: Se dice que solo las ceremonias de Machitún y una buena machi pueden hacer escapar del cuerpo a este ser

claims.statement: In Creole popular tradition it is said that to drive them away one must make metallic noises with spurs or other objects, in order to avoid a future misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi rakyat kreol dikatakan, untuk mengusir mereka orang harus membuat bunyi logam dengan taji atau benda lain agar terhindar dari malapetaka.
claims.quote: Igualmente en la tradición popular criolla, se dice que para ahuyentarlos hay que hacer ruidos metálicos con las espuelas u otros objetos, para así evitar una futura desgracia.

claims.statement: The Agropelter is a mythical fearsome critter said to live in hollow conifer trees from Maine to Oregon.
claims.statement_id: Agropelter adalah "fearsome critter" mitos yang konon menghuni pohon berongga di hutan konifer dari Maine hingga Oregon.
claims.quote: is a mythical fearsome critter said to inhabit hollow trees of the conifer woods from Maine to Oregon.

claims.statement: From there it waits for unwary people and hurls splinters and branches at them.
claims.statement_id: Dari sana ia menunggu orang yang lengah lalu melemparinya dengan serpihan kayu dan dahan.
claims.quote: From this vantage point, the creature would await an unwary person and hurl wooden splinters and branches at the intruder.

claims.statement: When loggers died from falling branches, the agropelter was blamed.
claims.statement_id: Saat penebang kayu tewas tertimpa dahan, agropelter dituduh melemparkannya.
claims.quote: When loggers died from branches falling on their heads, the agropelter was blamed for throwing the heavy branches.

claims.statement: In this text the agropelter leads a vengeful existence, resenting the intrusion of the logger, and deals misery to the lumber jack from Maine to Oregon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks ini, agropelter menjalani hidup penuh dendam dan membenci kehadiran penebang kayu, serta mendatangkan celaka bagi para penebang dari Maine sampai Oregon.
claims.quote: Leading a vengeful existence, resenting the intrusion of the logger, the agropelter deals misery to the lumber jack from Maine to Oregon.

claims.statement: Ill fares the man who tries to pass a hollow tree where one of these creatures has taken up temporary abode; the victim is usually found smashed or pinned by a dead branch and reported as killed by a falling limb.
claims.statement_id: Celakalah orang yang mencoba melewati pohon berongga tempat makhluk ini tinggal sementara; korbannya biasanya ditemukan remuk atau tertindih dahan mati dan dilaporkan tewas tertimpa dahan.
claims.quote: Ill fares the man who attempts to pass a hollow tree in which one of these creatures has taken up its temporary abode. The unfortunate is usually found smashed or pinned by a dead branch and reported as having been killed by a falling limb.

claims.statement: According to Ole, the animal has a slender, wiry body, the villainous face of an ape, and arms like muscular whiplashes with which it can snap off dead branches and hurl them through the air like shells from a six-inch gun.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ole, hewan itu bertubuh ramping dan liat, berwajah jahat seperti kera, dengan lengan seperti cambuk berotot yang dapat mematahkan dahan mati dan melemparkannya di udara seperti peluru meriam enam inci.
claims.quote: According to Ole, the animal has a slender, wiry body, the villainous face of an ape, and arms like muscular whiplashes, with which it can snap off dead branches and hurl them through the air like shells from a six-inch gun.

claims.statement: It is supposed to feed upon hoot owls and woodpeckers, the scarcity of which will always prevent the agropelter from becoming numerous in any locality.
claims.statement_id: Ia diduga makan burung hantu dan pelatuk, yang kelangkaannya akan selalu mencegah agropelter menjadi banyak di suatu tempat.
claims.quote: It is supposed to feed upon hoot owls and woodpeckers, the scarcity of which will always prevent the agropelter from becoming numerous in any locality.

claims.statement: Its pups are born on February 29 and always arrive in odd numbers.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anaknya lahir pada 29 Februari dan selalu berjumlah ganjil.
claims.quote: Its pups are born on February 29 and always arrive in odd numbers.

claims.statement: In one account, an agropelter kidnapped a pioneer surveyor and fed him raw fish until he escaped.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, seekor agropelter menculik seorang surveyor perintis dan memberinya ikan mentah sampai ia berhasil kabur.
claims.quote: In one account, an agropelter kidnapped a pioneer surveyor and fed him raw fish until he escaped.

claims.statement: Some have described the creature as being so quick that it has never been seen.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian menggambarkan makhluk ini begitu cepat sehingga tidak pernah terlihat.
claims.quote: Some have described the creature as being so quick that it has never been seen.

claims.statement: Atabey is an ancestral mother of the Taíno, one of two supreme ancestral spirits of Taíno mythology.
claims.statement_id: Atabey adalah ibu leluhur orang Taíno, salah satu dari dua roh leluhur tertinggi dalam mitologi Taíno.
claims.quote: Atabey is an ancestral mother of the Taíno, one of two supreme ancestral spirits in Taíno mythology.

claims.statement: She is a goddess of the moon, fresh waters, fertility and creation.
claims.statement_id: Ia dewi yang dikaitkan dengan bulan, air tawar, kesuburan, dan penciptaan.
claims.quote: She is a goddess associated with the moon, fresh waters, fertility and creation

claims.statement: Her manifestations include the nurturing mother, Caguana the spirit of love, and Guabancex, violent mother of storms, volcanoes and earthquakes.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya antara lain sosok ibu pengasuh, Caguana sang roh cinta, dan Guabancex, ibu badai, gunung api, dan gempa yang ganas.
claims.quote: One is the aforementioned nurturing maternal figure. Another is Caguana, the spirit of love. The last is Guabancex (also known as Gua Ban Ceh), the violent, wild mother of storms, volcanoes, and earthquakes.

claims.statement: Other names include Iermaoakar, Apito and Sumaiko; Taíno women prayed to her for safe childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Nama lain Atabey antara lain Iermaoakar, Apito, dan Sumaiko; perempuan Taíno berdoa kepadanya demi persalinan yang selamat.
claims.quote: Alternate names for Atabey include Iermaoakar, Apito, and Sumaiko. Taíno women prayed to Atabey to ensure safe childbirth.

claims.statement: She is the female entity who represents the spirit of all horizontal water: lakes, streams, the sea and the marine tides.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah sosok perempuan yang mewakili roh segala air mendatar: danau, sungai kecil, laut, dan pasang surut laut.
claims.quote: she is the female entity who represents the spirit of all horizontal water, lakes, streams, the sea, and the marine tides.

claims.statement: Atabey conceived a child without intercourse.
claims.statement_id: Atabey mengandung seorang anak tanpa persetubuhan.
claims.quote: Atabey conceived a child without intercourse.

claims.statement: She is still worshipped by many neo-Taino communities in the Spanish West Indies.
claims.statement_id: Ia masih dipuja oleh banyak komunitas neo-Taino di Hindia Barat Spanyol.
claims.quote: and is still worshipped by many neo-Taino communities in the Spanish West Indies.

claims.statement: Yúcahu was the supreme deity or zemi of the Pre-Columbian Taíno people along with his mother Atabey, who was his feminine counterpart.
claims.statement_id: Yúcahu adalah dewa tertinggi atau zemi orang Taíno pra-Columbus bersama ibunya, Atabey, yang menjadi pasangan feminin baginya.
claims.quote: He was the supreme deity or zemi of the Pre-Columbian Taíno people along with his mother Atabey who was his feminine counterpart.

claims.statement: In Innu mythology, Atshen is a cannibalistic spirit that hunts across the permafrost.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Innu, Atshen adalah roh kanibal yang berburu di tanah beku abadi.
claims.quote: In Innu mythology, Atshen is a cannibalistic spirit that hunts through the permafrost.

claims.statement: Atshen are a class of giant beings who were once human but were transformed into cannibals with no lips and hair on their hearts after they consumed human flesh.
claims.statement_id: Atshen adalah golongan makhluk raksasa yang dulunya manusia tetapi berubah menjadi kanibal tanpa bibir dan berambut di jantungnya setelah memakan daging manusia.
claims.quote: Atshen — a class of giant beings who were once human but were transformed into cannibals with no lips and hair on their hearts after they consumed human flesh;

claims.statement: Spirits such as Atshen and Memekueshu no longer appear to have a contemporary existence except in myths and legendary accounts; Atshen disappeared with the arrival of Christian missionaries.
claims.statement_id: Roh seperti Atshen dan Memekueshu tampaknya tidak lagi punya keberadaan masa kini kecuali dalam mitos dan kisah legenda; Atshen menghilang dengan datangnya misionaris Kristen.
claims.quote: Other spirits such as Atshen and Memekueshu no longer appear to have any contemporary existence except in myths and legendary accounts. As noted previously, Atshen disappeared with the arrival of Christian missionaries.

claims.statement: In the shaking tent, a shaman sometimes waged terrible battles with other shamans and cannibal spirits such as Atshen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tenda bergetar, dukun kadang bertempur hebat dengan dukun lain dan roh kanibal seperti Atshen.
claims.quote: or waged terrible battles there with other shamans and cannibal spirits such as Atshen.

claims.statement: In one myth, some members of a hunting group are labelled Atshen (cannibal monsters) because they have an abundance of food on their scaffold while the other members have none and are hungry.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu mitos, sebagian anggota kelompok pemburu disebut Atshen (monster kanibal) karena mereka punya banyak makanan di panggungnya sementara anggota lain kelaparan.
claims.quote: In one myth, for example, some members of a hunting group are labelled Atshen (i.e. cannibal monsters) because they have an abundance of food on their scaffold while the other members of the group have none and are hungry.

claims.statement: According to the author, one symbolic role of the Atshen in this myth seems to be to protect the caribou from excessive exploitation by the Innu, but the end result of the Atshens' intervention is starvation among the Innu.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis, tampaknya salah satu peran simbolis Atshen dalam mitos itu adalah melindungi karibu dari pemanfaatan berlebihan oleh orang Innu, tetapi hasil akhir campur tangan mereka adalah kelaparan di kalangan Innu.
claims.quote: It would seem that one symbolic role of the Atshen in this myth is to protect the caribou from excessive exploitation by the Innu, but the end result of Atshens' intervention is starvation among the Innu.

claims.statement: The axehandle hound is a fearsome critter of Minnesota and Wisconsin.
claims.statement_id: Axehandle hound adalah "fearsome critter" dari Minnesota dan Wisconsin.
claims.quote: is a fearsome critter of Minnesota and Wisconsin.

claims.statement: It is dog-like with an axe-shaped body.
claims.statement_id: Hewan ini mirip anjing dengan tubuh menyerupai kapak.
claims.quote: The animal is dog-like with a body which resembles an axe.

claims.statement: It eats only the handles of axes left unattended.
claims.statement_id: Makanannya hanya gagang kapak yang ditinggal tanpa pengawasan.
claims.quote: It subsists on a diet consisting entirely of the handles of axes which have been left unattended.

claims.statement: According to folklore it strongly dislikes red oak axe handles.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, ia sangat tidak suka gagang kapak dari kayu ek merah.
claims.quote: According to folklore, the axehandle hound strongly dislikes axe handles made from red oak.

claims.statement: A nocturnal creature, the axehandle hound travels from camp to camp searching for its next meal.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai makhluk nokturnal, axehandle hound berpindah dari kemah ke kemah mencari santapan berikutnya.

claims.statement_id: Ball-tailed cat adalah "fearsome critter" Amerika Utara yang mirip singa gunung, tetapi berekor sangat panjang dengan gumpalan padat di ujungnya untuk memukul mangsa.

claims.statement: Ball-tailed cat tales were common among woodsmen around the turn of the 20th century.

claims.statement: The earliest written mention is in Henry Tyron's Fearsome Critters (1939).

claims.quote: The earliest written mention of the ball-tailed cat appears in Henry Tyron's Fearsome Critters (1939).

claims.statement: Two of the more prominent variants are the Dingmaul and the Sliver Cat; the latter is distinguishable for having not only a smooth-sided ball for knocking wayfarers unconscious but also a spiked side for piercing and grappling its victims.

claims.statement: In Missouri folklore, the Beaman Monster is named after the town of Beaman.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Missouri, Beaman Monster adalah makhluk yang dinamai menurut kota Beaman.
claims.quote: In Missouri folklore, the Beaman Monster is an entity named after the town of Beaman.

claims.statement: Some call it the offspring of a 12-foot gorilla escaped from a circus train; others say it is "shaped like a wolf or coyote".
claims.statement_id: Sebagian menyebutnya keturunan gorila setinggi 12 kaki yang lolos dari kereta sirkus, sebagian lain menyebutnya berbentuk seperti serigala atau koyote.
