claims.statement: The Bear Lake Monster is an urban legend of a lake monster near Bear Lake on the Utah–Idaho border.
claims.statement_id: Bear Lake Monster adalah legenda urban tentang monster danau di sekitar Bear Lake, perbatasan Utah dan Idaho.
claims.quote: The Bear Lake Monster is a lake monster urban legend which appears in folklore near Bear Lake, on the Utah–Idaho border.

claims.statement: The myth grew from 19th-century articles by Joseph C. Rich, a Latter-day Saint settler, who later recanted them.
claims.statement_id: Mitos ini tumbuh dari artikel abad ke-19 karya Joseph C. Rich, pemukim Orang Suci Zaman Akhir, yang kemudian menarik kembali ceritanya.
claims.quote: The myth originally grew from articles written in the 19th century by Joseph C. Rich, a Latter-day Saint settler in the area, purporting to report second-hand accounts of sightings of the creature. However, he later recanted the stories.

claims.statement: It is now a tourist attraction; the last reported sighting was in 2002.
claims.statement_id: Kini monster ini dianggap daya tarik wisata; penampakan terakhir dilaporkan pada tahun 2002.
claims.quote: In recent years, the monster has been considered a tourist attraction. The last reported sighting of the monster was in 2002.

claims.statement: Folklorists say it resembles a serpent with legs about eighteen inches long, roaming the shore.
claims.statement_id: Menurut para folklorist, ia mirip ular tetapi berkaki sekitar delapan belas inci yang dipakainya berkeliaran di tepi danau.
claims.quote: is reported to resemble a serpent, but with legs about eighteen inches [46 cm] long on which it marauds along the shoreline.

claims.statement: The origins of the legend most likely stem from Shoshone stories of large serpents living in the lake, and the tale grew after Joseph C. Rich, a Mormon church leader, reported second-hand accounts of sightings of a snake-like creature in the lake in 1868.
claims.statement_id: Asal legenda ini kemungkinan besar berasal dari kisah suku Shoshone tentang ular besar di danau itu, dan kisah Bear Lake Monster berkembang setelah Joseph C. Rich, pemimpin gereja Mormon, melaporkan kabar dari tangan kedua tentang penampakan makhluk mirip ular di danau pada 1868.
claims.quote: While the origins of this regional legend most likely stem from Shoshone stories of large serpents living in the lake, the tale of the Bear Lake Monster grew after Joseph C. Rich, a Mormon church leader, reported second-hand accounts of sightings of a snake-like creature in the lake in 1868.

claims.statement: Rich later recanted his reports, admitting they were crafted as a marketing ploy to get people to visit Rich County, Utah.
claims.statement_id: Rich kemudian menarik laporannya dan mengakui bahwa laporan itu dibuat sebagai siasat pemasaran untuk menarik orang berkunjung ke Rich County, Utah.
claims.quote: Rich later recanted his reports, admitting they were crafted as a marketing ploy in attempts to get people to visit Rich County, Utah.

claims.statement: For community members the story serves as a sort of cautionary water tale as well as a fondly recalled local anecdote.
claims.statement_id: Bagi warga setempat, kisah ini berfungsi sebagai semacam dongeng peringatan tentang air sekaligus anekdot lokal yang dikenang dengan hangat.
claims.quote: the story serves for community members as a sort of cautionary water tale as well as a fondly recalled local anecdote.

claims.statement: Others reported a monster-like creature faster than a locomotive whose head was variously described as like that of a cow, otter, crocodile or a walrus (minus the tusks).
claims.statement_id: Yang lain melaporkan makhluk mirip monster yang bergerak lebih cepat daripada lokomotif, dengan kepala yang digambarkan beragam: mirip sapi, berang-berang, buaya, atau walrus (tanpa taring).
claims.quote: Others reported seeing a monster-like creature which went faster than a locomotive and had a head variously described as being similar to that of a cow, otter, crocodile or a walrus (minus the tusks).

claims.statement: The number of alleged lake-monster appearances across northern Utah led some people to speculate about an underground channel connecting the Great Salt Lake and other waterways to Bear Lake.
claims.statement_id: Banyaknya dugaan penampakan monster danau di seluruh Utah utara membuat sebagian orang menduga ada saluran bawah tanah yang menghubungkan Great Salt Lake dan perairan lain dengan Bear Lake.
claims.quote: The number of alleged appearances of lake monsters all across northern Utah caused some people to speculate that there was an underground channel connecting the Great Salt Lake and other waterways to Bear Lake.

claims.statement: Interest was high enough that LDS Church president Brigham Young decided to investigate whether the story was "an honest tale of a serpent or only a fish story" and sent a large rope to Paris, Idaho to aid in capturing the monster.
claims.statement_id: Minat begitu tinggi sehingga presiden Gereja LDS Brigham Young pernah memutuskan menyelidiki klaim itu untuk mengetahui apakah ceritanya "kisah jujur tentang ular atau sekadar cerita ikan", dan mengirim tali besar ke Paris, Idaho untuk membantu menangkap monster itu.
claims.quote: Interest was high enough that at one point even LDS Church president Brigham Young decided to investigate the claims to find out whether the story was "an honest tale of a serpent or only a fish story" and went as far as sending a large rope to Paris, Idaho to aid in capturing the monster.

claims.statement: Twenty-six years after his articles and allegations, Joseph C. Rich finally admitted that it had all been a "wonderful first-class lie".
claims.statement_id: Dua puluh enam tahun setelah artikel dan tuduhannya, Joseph C. Rich akhirnya mengakui bahwa semuanya adalah "kebohongan kelas satu yang luar biasa".
claims.quote: Twenty-six years following his articles and allegations, Joseph C. Rich finally admitted that it had all been a "wonderful first-class lie".

claims.statement: The legend of the Bufeo Colorado (Portuguese: Boto) comes from northern Brazil and is widespread in the Amazon rainforest.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Bufeo Colorado (bahasa Portugis: Boto) berasal dari Brasil utara dan tersebar luas di hutan hujan Amazon.
claims.quote: Die Legende des Bufeo Colorado (portugiesisch: Boto, französisch: Bouto) stammt aus dem Norden Brasiliens und ist im Amazonas-Regenwald weit verbreitet.

claims.statement: The legend concerns the Amazon river dolphins, the "pink river dolphins" of the Amazon and its tributaries.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini tentang lumba-lumba Amazon, atau "lumba-lumba sungai merah muda", yang hidup di Amazon dan anak-anak sungainya.
claims.quote: Die Legende handelt von den Amazonasdelfinen, auch „Rosa Flussdelfine“ genannt, welche im Amazonas und seinen Nebenflüssen leben.

claims.statement: The legend commonly explains pregnancies outside marriage and was filmed in the Brazilian film "Ele, o Boto" (1987).
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini biasanya dipakai untuk menjelaskan kehamilan di luar nikah dan difilmkan dalam film Brasil "Ele, o Boto" (1987).
claims.quote: Die Legende dient gemeinhin zur Erklärung außerehelicher Schwangerschaften und wurde 1987 im brasilianischen Film „Ele, o Boto“ verfilmt.

claims.statement: The Boto is said to appear at local festivals and dances as an elegant young man dressed in white.
claims.statement_id: Konon Boto muncul di pesta dan tarian setempat dalam wujud pemuda elegan berpakaian putih.
claims.quote: Es wird erzählt, dass der Boto während lokaler Festlichkeiten und Tänze in Gestalt eines eleganten, weiß gekleideten jungen Mannes erscheint.

claims.statement: He always wears a hat to hide the blowhole that remains on his head in human form.
claims.statement_id: Ia selalu memakai topi untuk menyembunyikan lubang napas di kepalanya yang tetap ada meski ia berwujud manusia.
claims.quote: Er trägt dabei stets einen Hut, um das verräterische Blasloch zu verstecken, das trotz der Verwandlung in einen Menschen auf seinem Kopf zurückbleibt.

claims.statement: So unknown young men arriving at a festival in a hat are asked to take it off.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu pemuda tak dikenal yang datang ke pesta bertopi diminta melepas topinya.
claims.quote: Aus diesem Grund werden unbekannte junge Männer, die mit Hut auf einem Fest erscheinen, gebeten, diesen abzunehmen.

claims.statement: The cabra cabriola ("leaping nanny goat") is a bogeyman of Portuguese myth told to children, also known elsewhere in Iberia and Brazil.
claims.statement_id: Cabra cabriola ("kambing betina yang melompat") adalah makhluk penakut anak dari mitos Portugis, juga dikisahkan di bagian lain Semenanjung Iberia dan Brasil.
claims.quote: is an imaginary bogeyman type being from Portuguese myth told to children, whose legend is also told in other parts of the Iberian Peninsula and Brazil.

claims.statement: It is imagined as a fire-breathing, sharp-toothed, goat-like, child-eating beast.
claims.statement_id: Ia dibayangkan sebagai binatang mirip kambing yang menyemburkan api, bergigi tajam, dan memakan anak-anak.
claims.quote: It is imagined to be a fire-breathing, sharp toothed, but goat-like, child-eating beast.

claims.statement: It is a bogeyman that frightens children into good behavior.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap monster penakut agar anak-anak berperilaku baik.
claims.quote: The cabra cabriola is considered a bogeyman monster that terrifies children into good behavior.

claims.statement: The cabra cabriola is said to be a man-eating goat that leaps and bucks a thousand times (hence the name, from cabriolar "to prance, caper").
claims.statement_id: Cabra cabriola dikatakan kambing pemakan manusia yang melompat dan menyepak seribu kali (karena itu namanya, dari cabriolar "melompat-lompat").
claims.quote: The cabra cabriola is said to be a man-eating goat, said to leap and buck a thousand times (hence the name, from cabriolar "to prance, caper").

claims.statement: It is said to be armed with huge jaws and sharp teeth used to devour youngsters, breathing fire from its eyes, mouth and nostrils.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan bersenjatakan rahang besar dan gigi tajam untuk melahap anak-anak, dan menyemburkan api dari mata, mulut, dan lubang hidungnya.
claims.quote: It is said to be armed with huge jaws and sharp teeth used to devour youngsters, breathing fire from its eyes, mouth, and nostrils

claims.statement: In one narrative the beast hides until the mother returns and learns her manner of speech, then goes to the blacksmith to re-forge its tongue to replicate the woman's soft voice.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, binatang itu bersembunyi menunggu sang ibu pulang dan mempelajari cara bicaranya, lalu pergi ke pandai besi untuk menempa ulang lidahnya agar dapat meniru suara lembut perempuan itu.
claims.quote: Undeterred, the beast hides in wait until the mother returns, and learns the manner of her speech, then goes to the blacksmith to re-forge his tongue in order to replicate the woman's soft voice.

claims.statement: In one tale, though tiny, the ant stung the cabra cabriola on the belly and it fled in pain screaming "baa, baa".
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, semut yang kecil menyengat perut cabra cabriola dan makhluk itu lari kesakitan sambil mengembik.
claims.quote: Though tiny, the ant stung the cabra cabriola on the belly and it fled in pain screaming: baa, baa.

claims.statement: Gilberto Freyre conjectures that the origins of the cabra cabriola may be traced back to the lore of the Caprimulgus (nightjar, literally "goat-milker").
claims.statement_id: Gilberto Freyre menduga asal-usul cabra cabriola dapat ditelusuri ke cerita rakyat tentang Caprimulgus (burung cabak, secara harfiah "pemerah kambing").
claims.quote: Gilberto Freyre conjectures that the origins of the cabra cabriola may be traced back to the lore of the Caprimulgus (nightjar, but literally "goat-milker")

claims.statement: Cabra Cabriola is a legend told mainly in Pernambuco and originating at the end of the 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Cabra Cabriola adalah legenda yang terutama diceritakan di Pernambuco dan berasal dari akhir abad ke-19.
claims.quote: Lenda da Cabra Cabriola ... contada principalmente em Pernambuco e teve origem no fim do

claims.statement: This character is half goat, half monster, with sharp teeth and a foul smell.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini setengah kambing, setengah monster, bergigi tajam, dan berbau busuk.
claims.quote: metade cabra, metade monstro, possui dentes afiados e um cheiro

claims.statement: It keeps searching for children to feed on, but also attacks people walking alone in the streets at night.
claims.statement_id: Ia terus mencari anak-anak untuk dimakan, tetapi juga menyerang orang yang berjalan sendirian di jalan pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Ela vive procurando por ... para se alimentar, mas ... ataca pessoas que andam nas ruas sozinhas durante a noite.

claims.statement: The goat (o caprino) is said to have the ability (habilidade) to enter houses (nas casas) in search of disobedient boys (meninos desobedientes).
claims.statement_id: Kambing itu (o caprino) dikatakan mampu (habilidade) masuk ke rumah-rumah (nas casas) untuk mencari anak laki-laki yang nakal (meninos desobedientes).
claims.quote: o caprino ... a habilidade de entrar nas casas a procura de meninos desobedientes.

claims.statement: Chaneque are legendary creatures of Mexican folklore; in Nahuatl the name means "those who inhabit dangerous places" or "owners of the house".
claims.statement_id: Chaneque adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Meksiko; dalam bahasa Nahuatl namanya berarti "mereka yang menghuni tempat berbahaya" atau "pemilik rumah".
claims.quote: are legendary creatures in Mexican folklore, meaning "those who inhabit dangerous places" or "owners of the house" in Náhuatl.

claims.statement: These small sprite-like beings are tied to elemental forces and seen as guardians of nature.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk kecil mirip peri ini terhubung dengan kekuatan alam dan dianggap penjaga alam.
claims.quote: These small, sprite-like beings hold a connection to elemental forces and are regarded as guardians of nature.

claims.statement: Modern legends portray them as children with elderly faces who can lead people astray for days.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda masa kini, chaneque digambarkan seperti anak kecil berwajah orang tua yang dapat menyesatkan orang selama berhari-hari.
claims.quote: In some contemporary legends, chaneques are portrayed as children with the faces of elderly men or women, capable of leading people astray for several days.

claims.statement: Elsewhere they frighten intruders until their souls leave their bodies.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah lain, chaneque menakut-nakuti penyusup hingga jiwa mereka meninggalkan tubuh.
claims.quote: In other instances, chaneques are said to intimidate intruders to the point where their souls leave their bodies.

claims.statement: The Colo Colo is an evil rat-like creature of Mapuche mythology.
claims.statement_id: Colo Colo adalah makhluk jahat mirip tikus dari mitologi Mapuche.
claims.quote: The Colo Colo or Colocolo is an evil rat-like creature from Mapuche mythology.

claims.statement: It nests near homes, sneaks in and drains blood or saliva from sleepers, causing weakness or tuberculosis.
claims.statement_id: Ia bersarang dekat rumah, menyelinap masuk, dan mengisap darah atau air liur orang tidur sehingga menyebabkan lemah atau tuberkulosis.
claims.quote: The Colo Colo is reputed to nest near a residence and sneak in, drinking blood from a sleeping resident, extracting saliva or licking utensils, causing debilitating weakness or tuberculosis.

claims.statement: It hatches from a stunted "rooster's egg"; the young is snake- or lizard-like and later becomes a feathered rat.
claims.statement_id: Ia menetas dari "telur ayam jantan" yang kerdil; anaknya mirip ular atau kadal, lalu berubah menjadi tikus berbulu.
claims.quote: It is often said to hatch from a stunted-looking "rooster's egg", and the young resembles a snake or burrowing lizard, but it later metamorphoses into a feathered rat form.

claims.statement: A wildcat is also called "colocolo", perhaps related to the lore's origin.
claims.statement_id: Sejenis kucing liar juga disebut "colocolo", yang mungkin terkait asal-usul cerita ini.
claims.quote: A type of wildcat is also called "colocolo", and this may perhaps be related to the origin of the lore.

claims.statement: In Mapuche oral tales, the Kolo-Kolo (this source's spelling of the figure also written Colo Colo) is said to derive from the work of the kalku and to bring all kinds of misfortune to those who see it: illness, suffering and sometimes death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam relato lisan Mapuche, Kolo-Kolo (ejaan sumber ini untuk sosok yang juga ditulis Colo Colo) dikatakan berasal dari perbuatan para kalku dan membawa segala macam malang bagi yang melihatnya: penyakit, penderitaan, dan kadang kematian.
claims.quote: se manifiesta y reconoce la figura del Kolo-Kolo, quien derivaría de la obra de los kalku y que, específicamente, daría toda clase de malaventuras a quienes lo ven: enfermedades, sufrimientos y, en algunos casos, hasta ocasionar la muerte.

claims.statement: The Kolo-Kolo usually hides in the ground and always acts in dark places; it is said to govern other beings of its kind and is seen as a chief or king.
claims.statement_id: Kolo-Kolo biasanya bersembunyi di dalam tanah dan selalu bertindak di tempat gelap; konon ia memerintah makhluk lain sejenisnya dan dipandang sebagai pemimpin atau raja.
claims.quote: Por lo regular se oculta en la tierra, actuando siempre en lugares oscuros. Se dice que gobierna a otros seres de su misma especie, percibiéndosele como jefe o rey.

claims.statement: In versions gathered in the Imperial sector, there is agreement in picturing it as a mouse covered in feathers, sometimes a lizard, or a small bird.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi yang dikumpulkan di sektor Imperial, ada kesepakatan membayangkannya sebagai tikus berbulu burung, kadang kadal, atau burung kecil.
claims.quote: en versiones recogidas en el sector de Imperial, habría consenso en visualizarlo como un ratón cubierto de plumas, a veces como un lagarto, o bien, como un pájaro pequeño.

claims.statement: Although its form is perceived differently, there is consensus on its function: extracting blood and saliva from people, thereby causing diseases such as consumption.
claims.statement_id: Meski wujudnya dipersepsikan berbeda-beda, ada kesepakatan mengenai fungsinya: menyedot darah dan air liur orang sehingga menimbulkan penyakit seperti tisis.
claims.quote: sí hay consenso en reconocer la función que desempeña: extraer sangre y saliva de las personas, originando, de ese modo, enfermedades como la tisis.

claims.statement: The figure is seen as a maleficent force that manifests in the mapu as a way of unbalancing the natural world.
claims.statement_id: Sosok itu dipandang sebagai kekuatan jahat yang tampil di mapu sebagai cara mengacaukan keseimbangan dunia alam.
claims.quote: fuerza maléfica que se manifiesta en el mapu como un modo de desequilibrar el mundo natural

claims.statement: Wayob is the plural of way (uay), a Maya word meaning 'sleep(ing)'; in Yucatec Maya it denotes the nagual, a person who turns into an animal while asleep to do harm, or that animal form itself.
claims.statement_id: Wayob adalah bentuk jamak dari way (uay), kata Maya yang berarti "tidur"; dalam bahasa Maya Yukatek, istilah ini menyebut nagual, orang yang berubah menjadi hewan saat tidur untuk berbuat jahat, atau wujud hewannya itu sendiri.
claims.quote: Wayob is the plural form of way (or uay), a Maya word with a basic meaning of 'sleep(ing)', but which in Yucatec Maya is a term specifically denoting the Mesoamerican nagual, that is, a person who can transform into an animal while asleep in order to do harm, or else the resulting animal transformation itself.

claims.statement: Already in Classic Maya belief, way animals, marked by a special hieroglyph, played an important role.

claims.statement: In Yucatec ethnography the animal form is usually a common domestic animal, but may be a ghost or apparition.
